# Downloading and Installing R and RStudio {#sec-downloading-r}

In order to use R on your computer, you will need both R and RStudio. Why both?

- *R* is the programming language itself. It does the actual work and runs the code.
- *RStudio* is the program we will use to write and work with R code.

One way to think about it: R is the language, while RStudio is the workspace where we write and use that language.

::: callout-tip
## Install R First!

You should install R before installing RStudio.
:::

## 1. Downloading and Installing R

R is free to download and is available for both Windows and Mac computers.

Choose the appropriate link for your computer:

- **Mac:** [Download R for macOS](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/macosx/)
- **Windows:** [Download R for Windows](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/base/)

After downloading the installer:

1.  Open the downloaded file.
2.  Follow the installation instructions.
3.  You can generally keep the **default installation options**.
4.  Allow the installation to finish.

::: callout-tip
### Don't touch R once it is installed!

You do not need to open or configure R after installing it. Once R is installed, you can move on to installing RStudio.
:::

## 2. Downloading and Installing RStudio

Next, we will install **RStudio**, which is where we will do most of our work throughout the course.

Use the link below to access the available RStudio downloads:

- [Download RStudio](https://docs.posit.co/ide/user/#rstudio-ide-oss-downloads)

Select the version that matches your computer and operating system.

![](images/rstudio-screenshot.png)

After downloading RStudio:

1.  Open the downloaded installer.
2.  Follow the installation instructions.
3.  You can generally keep the **default installation options**.
4.  Allow the installation to finish.

## 3. Make Sure Everything Works

Once **R and RStudio** are both installed, open **RStudio** (not **R**).

You should see several different sections of the RStudio window. Don't worry about understanding everything you see yet—we will learn how to use RStudio together.

Look for the **Console**, usually located on the left side of the RStudio window.

![](images/console-screenshot-02.png)

Next to the `>` symbol, type:

``` r
2 + 2
```

Press **Enter**.

You should see:

``` text
[1] 4
```

If you see `4`, congratulations! **R and RStudio are installed and working correctly.**

::: callout-note
### Having Trouble?

If RStudio does not open, you receive an error, or your screen looks very different from the examples in this guide, don't worry.

Take a screenshot of what you see so we can troubleshoot the issue together.
:::
